Subject: SLO & topology alignment — Xenon MedTech discovery deep-dive

Thanks again for the time this morning — great conversation. Below is a concise capture of the technical items we discussed, the pain we heard, and the concrete next steps we recommend. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain & goals
- Primary pain: unpredictable tail latency during peak inference (spikes to 1.2s P99) causing degraded user experience for clinicians.
- Business goal: sub-300ms P95 for single-turn summarization calls (avg ~600 input tokens) and steady throughput to support peak 100–150 concurrent active users.
- Compliance: data must remain in-customer VPC, with KMS-backed key control and audit logs retained for 12 months. SOC 2 evidence requested.

Technical readout (what we heard)
- Typical request profile: 600 tokens in, expecting ~150 tokens out on average; pre- and post-processing add ~30ms per call.
- Peak concurrency target: 120–140 QPS across three regions (primary in us-west).
- Current constraints: on-prem CPU-based model hosts; no KV cache for repeated prompts; caching would significantly lower cost & tail latency.

Proposed Redwood topology & configuration (initial recommendation)
- Deployment: Redwood Private control plane with a dedicated GPU pool in the customer VPC (NVIDIA H100-equivalent or A100 cluster) to meet deterministic latency.
- Model variant: start with an optimized 13B quantized variant (we recommended redwood-13b-8q) for a balance of throughput + quality; reserve option to switch to 70B-quant for higher-quality batches.
- Cache & batching: enable prefix KV caching for common templates + dynamic batching with a 20ms micro-batch window. Expect ~2–3x cost reduction on repeated prompts.
- Fallbacks: multi-variant routing — primary low-latency 13B; fallback to a cheaper 7B for non-critical background tasks.
- Observability: per-route P95/P99, token-cost tracing, and request id propagation to Xenon's logging stack.

SLOs we propose to target (first milestone)
- P95 latency (inference-only): <= 250ms for 600-token inputs.
- P99 latency (end-to-end): <= 800ms (includes preprocessing + network).
- Availability: 99.95% for the dedicated pool.

Immediate next steps (open items)
1) Xenon to share a 48-hour access log sample + a small request sample set (anonymized) — helps validate token distribution and cache hit opportunities. (Anika)
2) Redwood to produce an initial capacity sketch + rough cost estimate and a mutual action plan. (Marcus)
3) Security: exchange SOC 2 evidence and KMS integration checklist. (Laura)

Attachments: a quick sketch of the latency math and our working mutual action plan attached.

Thanks — will follow up with a short MPA and a calendar invite for an ops deep-dive next week.

— Marcus

Thanks Marcus — this is an excellent capture. A few clarifications / additions from our side:  

Clarifications
- Our peak concurrency is measured as user-facing interactions; eq. to ~120 sustained concurrent sessions, burstable to 220 for brief campaign spikes.
- Average total end-to-end budget per request: ~350–400ms; we are willing to trade a small increase in cost for tighter P95 but need P99 protections.

Model/Quality notes
- We ran internal evals showing that smaller quantized 13B variants meet our accuracy bar for note summarization in 78% of cases; for the remaining clinical-critical flows (discharge summaries) we need the 70B-class quality.

Security/compliance
- SOC 2: we can share the external auditor report and the list of relevant controls (will send by EOD).
- KMS/HSM: we use a customer-managed KMS in our VPC; any key wrap flow must be compatible.

Files attached: anonymized 48-hour trace (xenon_latency_report.pdf) + a draft mutual action plan spreadsheet (xenon_map_mutual_action_plan.xlsx).

Next actions from Xenon
- We’ll extract a 1,000-sample request set with annotations for caching candidates and share by Thursday. (Xavier)
- Confirm windows for ops deep-dive: prefer Thu 07/06 or Mon 07/10, morning PT. (Anika)

Appreciate the recommended topology — we like the idea of multi-variant routing with cache + micro-batching. Looking forward to the capacity sketch.

Best,
Anika
